page.layout: One column of running text. Marginal notes in the left margin, beside the lines they belong to. Running head at top right. Page number at top right of the head line.

main_text.l: calamitatum & miseriarum metus ac de-
nunciatio mœrore lenit: & idem miseri-
cordia præstat, demortuorum cognatorum,
vel aliorum qui cari fuerunt, [illegible, ~9 letters]
& obtestatione adhibita. Ad ἰδικά porrò
mo-rata & conciliatia argumenta quod attinet,
à perfona illa partim noftra, partim eorū
ad quos scribimus petitur. In noftra amo-
ris ac beneuolentię significatio: commemo-
ratio officiorū: societas ægritudinis: lite-
rarū, vel infrequentię, vel breuitatis excu-
satio: extenuatio viriū in consolando mo-
desta: metus etiā nonnunquam profesio
prodeft: ne temerè, vel cōfidere ipsi, vel ina-
nem aliis iniicere spē videamur. In aliena
laus vtilis est ac cōmendatio pietatis, do-
ctrinę, prudentię, magnitudinis animi: a-
moris itidem, studij, officij illius quē con-
solari cupimus: & hac ipsa quasi languen-
tes excitari solent.Sunt autem, vt de argume-
ntorum istorum collocatione atq; tractatio-
ne agamus, quatuor consolatoriarum epistolarum
partes: Exordium, propositio, confirma-
tio & conclusio. Exordia constant, vel
δείξει τῆς συμπαθείας [?] significatione doloris,
meroris, luctus ex amici casu aduerso per-
ceptì, & modesta virium atq; ingenij no-
stri in consolando extenuatione. lib. 1. e-pist.5.

marginalia.note: Collocatio argumentorum in singulis consolatoriarum epistolarum partibus.

page.notes: Greek words are uncertain: the word after "fuerunt," is illegible; "ἰδικά" in the note and text, and "δείξει τῆς συμπαθείας" in the Exordia note, are copied with [?] where the scan is faint. The left-margin note beginning "rum argu-" is partly cut off at its top. The reference "pist.5." at the foot is set right-aligned and read as "e-pist.5." after the hyphenated "e-" at the line end. No catchword or signature is visible.
